441	4. Mediator's `cross_topic_policy = "peek"`.
442	5. Tool descriptions: genericize universally; per-bot override only as escape hatch.
443	6. No "bridge" primitive — dropped.
444	7. Artifacts multi-topic via `topic_ids uuid[]` (array, not join table — keep simple).
445	8. **Writes do not force-include own topic.** Default is `[bot.primary_topic]`; agent fully overrides.

447	10. `participants_shape` on `BotSpec`: `solo` or `dyad`.
448	11. Explicit `dyads`, `dyad_members`, `bot_bindings`, `user_bot_state` tables.

454	- **I. `bridge_candidates` flow.** Closed. Verified structurally dyadic; needs `dyad_id` column for multi-bot. The "same bot orchestrating both sides" assumption *is* baked in (see §18.2). New open M below.

462	
463	D. **Solo bot's crisis escalation.** Refer to dyadic bot? Surface external resources? Different per bot — but we should pick a default for solo bots so each new one inherits sane behavior.
464	
465	E. **Cross-bot user identity across transports.** If one user reaches the coach via Discord and the mediator via WhatsApp, we need a way to know "same human." Current `users` has one `phone`. A `user_identities(user_id, transport, address)` table will be needed; probably phase 4+ but worth flagging.
466	
467	F. **`bot_id` column type.** `text` vs FK to `bots`. Recommend FK with `ON DELETE RESTRICT`.
468	
469	G. **Multi-transport bots.** A bot using both Discord and SMS would need per-channel transport config (not per-bot global). Probably out of scope until needed, but the abstraction should not preclude it.
470	
471	H. **Status-block cap in prompt budget.** If a user has bindings to many bots/topics, the status block grows. Cap at N most-recent topics? Document the rule and surface the rest behind `get_topic_status`.
472	
473	**New opens raised by verification:**
474	
475	K. **Solo bot support is structurally heavier than the doc implies.** Hot context (~10 dyad assumptions) and prompt renderer (dyad-only sections for cross-thread sharing, partner perspective, bridge candidates, in-person redirection, crisis escalation) cannot be made parametric cleanly. **Recommendation:** split into separate solo and dyadic `hot_context_builder` and `system_prompt_renderer` implementations on `BotSpec`. `TurnContext` types `partner: User` — make it `Optional[User]`, but the real work is in the two new builders/renderers. See §18.4, §18.5.
476	
477	L. **Distillations need a fourth scoping category.** Provenance (`source_user_ids[]`) is not about-whom. Tool-level write/read code already filters by `source_user_id = ANY(source_user_ids)`. The cross-thread visibility logic (`raw_message_visibility`) is dyad-shaped. For solo bots, distillations collapse to "this user's material" — single-entry array. For dyadic, current behavior preserved. See §18.1.
478	
479	M. **`bridge_candidates` need `dyad_id`.** Currently the schema is just `source_user_id`/`target_user_id` with no dyad anchor; the flow assumes a single `ctx` containing both sides. With multi-bot serving the same dyad through different bots (or different dyads), this leaks/breaks. Add `dyad_id` in phase 0. Decide later whether to add `topic_id`/`bot_id` as well. See §18.2.
480	
481	---
482	
483	## 18. Verification addendum (Codex pass, read-only)
484	
485	Findings from an independent read of the actual code, against the design in §1–17. Every claim cites file:line.
486	
487	### 18.1 `distillations` about-whom
488	
489	`distillations` are neither `about_user_id` nullable like memories/observations nor pair-only like themes. They are evidence/provenance-scoped via `source_user_ids uuid[] NOT NULL CHECK (cardinality(source_user_ids) > 0)` (`migrations/0015_distillations.sql:16`). Core columns are: `id`, `content`, encrypted content, `confidence`, `status`, `sensitivity`, `visibility`, `shareable_summary`, `source_user_ids`, related memory/observation/theme/message arrays, revision links/counts, and timestamps (`migrations/0015_distillations.sql:6-30`). Tool code enforces `source_user_ids` stay inside `ctx.user`/`ctx.partner`, not "about whom" (`app/services/tools/write_tools.py:568-576`), and inserts `source_user_ids` directly (`app/services/tools/write_tools.py:939-956`). Read filtering is also by `source_user_id = ANY(source_user_ids)` (`app/services/tools/read_tools.py:654-656`). Plan needs a fourth about/provenance shape.
490	
491	### 18.2 `bridge_candidates` end-to-end
492	
493	Schema is explicitly dyadic: `source_user_id`, `target_user_id`, `kind`, lifecycle `status`, `sensitivity`, `source_message_ids`, summaries, sent message, timestamps (`migrations/0013_bridge_candidates.sql:3-18`). `partner_path` later classifies the bridge route, defaulting historical rows to `message_partner` (`migrations/0016_partner_bridge_paths.sql:3-17`). Proposed by `create_bridge_candidate`; it requires `source_user_id == ctx.user.id` and both users in the current dyad (`app/services/tools/write_tools.py:273-286`, `app/services/tools/write_tools.py:504-506`). Status auto-derives `ready` only for opt-in low/medium source material, otherwise `pending` (`app/services/tools/write_tools.py:291-302`). Target surfacing happens in hot context only where `target_user_id = current user`, `source_user_id = partner`, `status='ready'`, and `partner_path='message_partner'` (`app/services/hot_context.py:424-438`). Target can only mark visible candidates `addressed` or `declined` (`app/services/tools/write_tools.py:348-371`). Immediate sending is source-side only and sends to `ctx.partner` (`app/services/tools/write_tools.py:437-487`). Multi-bot breaks unless bridge rows gain dyad/bot/topic scope: current code assumes the same bot has both partners in one `ctx`.
494	
495	### 18.3 `scheduled_jobs` vs `scheduled_tasks`
496	
497	There is no `scheduled_tasks` table. The active table is `scheduled_jobs` (`migrations/0001_init.sql:98-107`). Migration 0017 only adds `scheduled_task` as a `scheduled_jobs.job_type` plus indexes (`migrations/0017_scheduled_tasks.sql:3-24`). The worker claims and dispatches rows from `scheduled_jobs` only (`app/services/scheduled_jobs.py:104-138`). `scheduled_task` is an agent-managed job subtype handled by `handle_scheduled_task` (`app/services/scheduled_job_handlers.py:160-169`) and created/listed/updated/cancelled through `scheduled_jobs` rows (`app/services/tools/write_tools.py:1337-1374`, `app/services/tools/write_tools.py:1404-1472`). Recommendation: add `bot_id` and `topic_id` to `scheduled_jobs`; do not model `scheduled_tasks` as a parallel table.
498	
499	### 18.4 `hot_context` coupling
500	
501	`build_hot_context(pool, user, partner: User, ...)` is not partner-optional (`app/services/hot_context.py:173-179`). Passing `None` breaks immediately at `_user_profile(pool, partner)` (`app/services/hot_context.py:180-181`). Dyad assumptions are pervasive: OOB pulls both owners (`app/services/hot_context.py:227-235`), memories use `[user.id, partner.id]` plus shared NULL (`app/services/hot_context.py:248-258`), messages query either participant (`app/services/hot_context.py:328-339`), sharing defaults require both users (`app/services/hot_context.py:340-343`), distillations filter both source ids (`app/services/hot_context.py:344-360`), bridges require partner-as-source (`app/services/hot_context.py:424-438`), and render always emits "Your Partner" plus partner sharing defaults (`app/services/hot_context.py:581-608`). `TurnContext` also types `partner: User` (`app/services/turn_context.py:16-22`). A solo builder should be separate.
502	
503	### 18.5 Prompt renderer coupling
504	
505	The prompt opens as a relationship mediator between `{partner_a_name}` and `{partner_b_name}` (`app/services/prompts.py:7-12`). The renderer requires both `partner_a` and `partner_b` strings (`app/services/prompts.py:435-443`) and blindly replaces both placeholders (`app/services/prompts.py:464-471`). Large sections are dyad-only: cross-thread sharing, partner perspective, bridge candidates, in-person redirection, and crisis escalation to partner (`app/services/prompts.py:122-133`, `app/services/prompts.py:166-186`, `app/services/prompts.py:217-222`, `app/services/prompts.py:335-370`). Split solo vs dyadic renderers; making `partner` optional in this renderer would leave too much dead policy.
506	
507	### 18.6 OOB delivery-time guardrail
508	
509	Delivery-time OOB runs before `send_outbound` delivery via `_call_oob_hook(pool, content, user.id, protected_owner_ids)` (`app/services/messaging.py:338-366`) and for incremental parts at the same point (`app/services/messaging.py:193-228`). The default hook calls `check_oob_with_policy` (`app/services/hooks.py:13-25`). Scope defaults to recipient only when `protected_owner_ids` is omitted (`app/services/oob_check.py:106-109`, `app/services/oob_check.py:175-180`); agentic turns currently pass both dyad ids (`app/services/agentic.py:725-741`). The check fetches active OOB by owner/status only, no topic filter (`app/services/oob_check.py:112-124`). Adding `topic_ids IS NULL OR $bot_topic = ANY(topic_ids)` is moderate: schema first, then thread `bot_topic` through `send_outbound`, `_call_oob_hook`, hook contract, and `_active_oob_entries`. It is a separate Anthropic model call, not in-process logic (`app/services/oob_check.py:191-221`).
510	
511	### 18.7 Outbound transport coupling
512	
513	Transport is globally selected from `settings.messaging_provider` (`app/config.py:26`). `send_outbound` branches inline on provider and directly calls `discord.send_text` or `whatsapp.send_text/send_template` (`app/services/messaging.py:370-399`). Incremental sending is Discord-only and returns `not_enabled` for any other provider (`app/services/messaging.py:155-168`). There is no sender interface. Per-bot outbound is moderate, not trivial: introduce a transport/channel object, move provider/window/template behavior behind it, and stamp message rows with bot/channel.
514	
515	### Findings that change the plan
516	
517	- `distillations` need explicit provenance-vs-about modeling; the current table does not fit the doc's two existing about-whom categories.
518	- `scheduled_tasks` should be removed from the schema plan as a separate concept; it is a `scheduled_jobs` subtype.
519	- Solo support is not a signature tweak. Hot context, prompt rendering, turn context, and bridge tools are structurally dyadic.
520	- Bridge candidates need `dyad_id` plus likely `bot_id/topic_id`; current source/target-only rows will leak semantics across bots.
521	
522	---
523	
524	## 19. Adversarial review addendum (Codex gpt-5.5 high)
525	
526	Second-pass review at higher reasoning. Found issues missed by the first pass.
527	
528	### 19.1 Phase 0 is not truly "no behavior change"
529	
530	§15 says add `bot_id`/`topic_id`, backfill, then set NOT NULL. But current inserts don't write either column: inbound `messages` at `app/services/inbound.py:161`, outbound at `app/services/messaging.py:55` and `:84`, `bot_turns` at `app/services/agentic.py:483`. Either keep nullable+defaulted until phase 1, or phase 0 ships insert-site updates alongside schema. As written, phase 0 would break writes the moment NOT NULL applies.
531	
532	### 19.2 Bridge candidates need bot_id AND topic_id, not just dyad_id
533	
534	§17 M punted `bot_id`/`topic_id` to "later." That's wrong. `dyad_id` only prevents cross-dyad leakage. A coach and mediator sharing a dyad cannot share one bridge queue without bot/topic scope — the bot reading bridges needs to filter to its own.
535	
536	### 19.3 "Axis A collapses for solo bots" is aspirational
537	
538	Tool schemas at `tool_schemas.py:815, 884, 954, 1041` accept raw `about_user_id`, `owner_user_id`, `source_user_ids`, OOB `owner_id` with no binding-shape validation. "Solo bot never picks shared" is not an invariant unless tools reject illegal scopes structurally.
539	
540	### 19.4 TurnContext is the dependency hub the doc under-specifies
541	
542	`app/services/turn_context.py:16` has `user`, mandatory `partner`, message ids, hot context, OOB owners. No `bot_id`, `topic_id`, `binding_id`, `channel_id`, or `participants_shape`. `_run_agentic` constructs it after resolving `settings.bot_id` at `agentic.py:678`. Every scope decision must live on `TurnContext` or every tool rediscovers it — or worse, trusts the model.
543	
544	### 19.5 Newer-inbound suppression is per-user, not per-(user, bot)
545	
546	`_newer_inbound_exists` at `agentic.py:612` suppresses sends by `sender_id` only; same in `send_message_part` at `read_tools.py:166`. Multi-bot breakage: a message to the finance bot cancels the mediator's final send. Bot/channel must be part of the suppression key.
547	
548	### 19.6 Global pause is deeper than per-(user, bot)
549	
550	`system_state.is_paused` at `system_state.py:23` reads a single `global_pause` key. Inbound pause supersedes scheduled jobs at `inbound.py:136`. Scheduler switches to heartbeat-only when globally paused at `scheduled_jobs.py:75`. Moving pause to `user_bot_state` is not a local refactor — the global pause primitive needs its own answer (kept as kill switch? per-bot heartbeat?).
551	
552	### 19.7 `consult_perspective` clones ctx without topic-awareness
553	
554	At `consult_perspective.py:105-139`, the consult clones the same ctx, partner, protected_owner_ids, hot context, and grants consult-phase reads. `cross_topic_policy` would have to be inherited structurally; prose alone won't gate it.
555	
556	### 19.8 Audit needs more than `bot_id` on `bot_turns`
557	
558	`bot_turns` stores `system_prompt_version` and `prompt_snapshot` but no bot identity. Adding `bot_id` is necessary but not enough: future audits will need `BotSpec` code version, prompt renderer version, tool schema version, and hot-context builder version per turn.
559	
560	### 19.9 Onboarding is hard-coded mediator-shaped
561	
562	Hard-coded mediator welcome at `inbound.py:23`. Global `users.onboarding_state` at `models/user.py:16`. First-contact prompt rendering keyed from that global state at `prompts.py:446`. Per-bot onboarding is broader than per-(user, bot) state: each bot needs its own welcome copy, first-turn behavior, and a migration story for users already welcomed by mediator.
563	
564	### 19.10 `topic_ids uuid[]` is the wrong durable shape
565	
566	Array column makes "who tagged this topic, when, why, with what confidence" impossible without rewriting the row. Per-topic lifecycle (retiring career relevance, keeping relationship relevance) is an opaque array edit with no audit trail. **Recommendation:** join table for artifacts that can truly be multi-topic. (Earlier we picked array for simplicity; that simplicity is paid for in lost audit fidelity.)
567	
568	### 19.11 "Agent can fully override topic on write" is ambient write authority
569	
570	§7's "agent fully overrides `topic_ids` on write" with no per-bot scope is not flexibility — it's unconstrained write authority across the system. Durable rule should be: default own topic, allow *configured* write scopes per bot, record reason for any cross-topic write.
571	
572	### 19.12 `topic_status` NULL = pair needs `dyad_id`
573	
574	Per `(topic, user)` with NULL = pair assumes one dyad. If two dyads share `relationship`, the pair-level rows collide. Add `dyad_id` (or `binding_id`) to `topic_status`.
575	
576	### 19.13 Status injection undermines `cross_topic_policy`
577	
578	§13 injects all topic statuses into every bot's system prompt. A bot with `cross_topic_policy="forbidden"` still sees sensitive headlines verbatim. Status injection must itself be policy-gated, not just cross-topic reads. Headlines will become tiny summaries of sensitive domains — verbatim leak is especially risky.
579	
580	### 19.14 Solo/dyad split is incomplete
581	
582	Splitting hot context and prompt renderer is right but not enough. Tool registry, allowed tools, OOB policy, bridge tools, escalation tools, scheduler handlers, and `TurnContext` type all need participant-shape-specific contracts. Otherwise solo bots hide dyad affordances in prompt text while the underlying tools remain callable.
583	
584	### 19.15 Authorization model is missing
585	
586	The doc has scope arguments but no explicit authorization. Which bot can read/write which topics, for which binding, under which participant shape? `scope="all"` is a parameter, not a permission. Needs to be expressed as policy on `BotSpec` (e.g. `read_scopes`, `write_scopes`) and enforced at the tool boundary.
587	
588	### 19.16 Channel identity / account-linking is phase 0/1, not phase 4
589	
590	Current `users.phone` is reused for Discord ids at `discord.py:176` against `migrations/0001_init.sql:10`. Multi-transport will break user identity before the second bot is useful. The doc punted this to "phase 4+" — that's wrong. Resolve identity model in phase 0 or 1.
591	
592	### 19.17 Other missing topics
593	
594	Per-bot spend caps. Per-bot eval baselines. Admin UI filters by bot. RLS/policy changes for topic-scoped access. Deletion/export semantics across topics (GDPR-shaped). Migration validation queries proving no unscoped rows remain after backfill.
595	
596	### 19.18 Most-dangerous open question: §17.E (cross-bot user identity)
597	
598	Routing, bindings, privacy, status injection, and topic sharing all rest on user identity. If we write memories/OOB/feedback under duplicate humans (one user known by two transport identifiers), retrofitting a merge later is privacy-sensitive and expensive — encrypted blobs reference user ids, audit logs would diverge, OOB scoping breaks. Not a phase 4 problem.
599	
600	### 19.19 Bottom line
601	
602	The doc has the right nouns but still treats multi-agent as "add columns and route through `BotSpec`." The hard part is enforcing scope at every site that currently assumes one dyad, one transport, one global pause, one prompt family, one conversation stream. Without binding-aware `TurnContext`, FK-backed `bot_id`, join-table topic membership, and explicit read/write authorization, this design ships as a leaky mediator with labels.
603

No partner concept. No pair-level status.\n- **Dyad**: serves two users. Each turn picks `user_in_context` (whoever just messaged). Writes can specify `about_user_id = A`, `B`, or `NULL` (shared). Pair-level status supported.\n\nThis single config decides whether the bot needs partner handling, shared-mode artifacts, dyadic crisis escalation, bridge candidates.\n\n### Enforcement, not aspiration (§19.3, §19.14)\n\n\"Solo bot never picks shared\" is not an invariant unless tools reject illegal scopes. Tool entry points validate against `TurnContext.participants_shape` and `TurnContext.binding`:\n\n- Solo bot calling a write with `about_user_id != bound_user.id` → rejected.\n- Solo bot calling a write with `about_user_id = NULL` (shared) → rejected.\n- Dyadic bot calling a write with `about_user_id` outside the bound dyad → rejected.\n\nTool registry has *participant-shape-specific contracts*. Bridge tools, in-person redirect, partner-perspective tools are only registered for dyadic bots — not \"registered everywhere and gated by prompt language.\" Solo bots literally cannot call them.\n\n### Bindings (data)\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE dyads (\n  id          uuid PRIMARY KEY,\n  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE dyad_members (\n  dyad_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES dyads(id),\n  user_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),\n  PRIMARY KEY (dyad_id, user_id)\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE bot_bindings (\n  id         uuid PRIMARY KEY,\n  bot_id     text NOT NULL REFERENCES bots(id),\n  user_id    uuid REFERENCES users(id),   -- set for solo\n  dyad_id    uuid REFERENCES dyads(id),   -- set for dyad\n  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),\n  CHECK ((user_id IS NOT NULL) <> (dyad_id IS NOT NULL))\n);\n```\n\nThe current implicit \"dyad in settings\" becomes an explicit `dyads` row in migration. Adding a second bot is then a new `bot_bindings` row.\n\n### Defaults on writes\n\n- **Solo bot**: `about_user_id` defaults to the bound user, validation enforces it.\n- **Dyadic bot**: `about_user_id` defaults to `user_in_context`. Agent can explicitly set partner or NULL when warranted, subject to authorization (§6).\n\n---\n\n## 6. Scope on `TurnContext` and the authorization model\n\nThe most under-specified surface in the prior drafts. Codex flagged both (§19.4, §19.15). This section is the spine.\n\n### 6.1 What `TurnContext` carries\n\nToday (`app/services/turn_context.py:16`): `user`, mandatory `partner`, message ids, hot context text, OOB owners. Adds:\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass TurnContext:\n    # existing\n    user: User\n    partner: User | None           # None for solo bots\n    triggering_message_ids: list[UUID]\n    hot_context: str\n    protected_owner_ids: list[UUID]\n    # added\n    bot_id: str\n    bot_spec: BotSpec\n    binding_id: UUID\n    participants_shape: Literal[\"solo\", \"dyad\"]\n    primary_topic_id: UUID\n    primary_topic_slug: str\n    channel_id: UUID\n    cross_topic_policy: Literal[\"peek\", \"explicit\", \"forbidden\"]\n    read_scopes: ReadScopes        # see §6.3\n    write_scopes: WriteScopes      # see §6.3\n```\n\nEvery tool call sees this. Every authorization check uses fields on this object, never `settings` and never the model's word.\n\n### 6.2 Resolution at turn start\n\nIn the inbound flow (§13.1), the runtime resolves: channel → bot → binding → primary topic → bot_spec → scopes. The fully-populated `TurnContext` is constructed once and passed to the agentic loop. No tool re-resolves any of this; no tool consults `settings`.\n\n### 6.3 Authorization model\n\nEach `BotSpec` declares scopes explicitly:\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ReadScopes:\n    topics: frozenset[str] | Literal[\"own\", \"all\"]  # own = primary only\n    allow_cross_topic_peek: bool                    # status counts of other topics\n    allow_cross_topic_status_injection: bool        # see §7.4\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass WriteScopes:\n    topics: frozenset[str]                         # always contains primary\n    require_reason_for_cross_topic: bool           # logged on write\n```\n\nThe mediator launches with `read_scopes = {\"own\", peek=True, status=True}` and `write_scopes = {\"relationship\"}`. A coach launches with `{\"career\"}`/`{\"career\"}` and `peek=True`. Cross-topic writes (a coach writing to the relationship topic) require an explicit `write_scopes` widening and a `reason` field on the write — which is recorded in `artifact_topics.reason`.\n\nThis replaces the previous \"agent can fully override `topic_ids`\" rule, which was unconstrained write authority masquerading as flexibility (§19.11).\n\n### 6.4 Enforcement points\n\n- **Read tools** consult `ctx.read_scopes` before filtering.\n- **Write tools** consult `ctx.write_scopes` before INSERT. Cross-topic writes require non-empty `reason`.\n- **Status injection** in hot context consults `ctx.read_scopes.allow_cross_topic_status_injection`. A `forbidden` bot does not see other topics' statuses in its prompt at all (§19.13).\n- **`consult_perspective`** clones `ctx` *preserving scopes*. Consult inherits the same authorization (§19.7).\n\n---\n\n## 7. Topic status\n\nShort headline + paragraph the agent maintains. Visible in every bot's system prompt (when authorized).\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE topic_status (\n  id                       uuid PRIMARY KEY,\n  topic_id                 uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES topics(id),\n  dyad_id                  uuid REFERENCES dyads(id),    -- set when pair-level\n  user_id                  uuid REFERENCES users(id),    -- set when per-user\n  headline                 text NOT NULL,\n  body                     text NOT NULL,\n  last_updated_at          timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),\n  last_updated_by_bot_id   text NOT NULL REFERENCES bots(id),\n  CHECK ((user_id IS NOT NULL) <> (dyad_id IS NOT NULL))\n);\nCREATE UNIQUE INDEX topic_status_user_key\n  ON topic_status (topic_id, user_id) WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL;\nCREATE UNIQUE INDEX topic_status_dyad_key\n  ON topic_status (topic_id, dyad_id) WHERE dyad_id IS NOT NULL;\n```\n\n### 7.1 Pair-level needs `dyad_id` (§19.12)\n\nPer `(topic, user)` with NULL=pair only worked if there were exactly one dyad. With multiple dyads the pair-level rows collide. Pair-level rows are now keyed by `(topic_id, dyad_id)`.\n\n### 7.2 Solo vs dyadic write rules\n\n- **Solo bot**: writes per-user statuses only, for its bound user.\n- **Dyadic bot**: writes per-user statuses for either partner *and* pair-level status (`dyad_id` set, `user_id` NULL).\n\n### 7.3 The tool\n\n```\nset_topic_status(scope, headline, body)\n  scope = \"user:<id>\" | \"pair\"\n```\n\nTopic is implicit from `ctx.primary_topic_id` (a bot can only update its own topic's status). Rejected at tool boundary if scope doesn't match bot shape.\n\n### 7.4 Status injection is policy-gated (§19.13)\n\nHot context normally injects all topic statuses for served user(s) and pair. But this respects `ctx.read_scopes.allow_cross_topic_status_injection`:\n\n- Bot with `peek` or `all`: sees its own topic's statuses + cross-topic statuses.\n- Bot with `forbidden`: sees only its own topic's statuses.\n\nStatus headlines will become tiny summaries of sensitive domains; verbatim cross-topic leakage is the exact failure mode the policy must guard.\n\n### 7.5 Status updates folded into `record`\n\nThe record-step instruction prompts the agent to call `set_topic_status` when the topic's status no longer reflects current reality. No new turn phase. Promote to its own phase only if telemetry shows agents forgetting.\n\n### 7.6 History deferred\n\n`topic_status_history` (append-only) added in a later phase when there's a UI or audit need for it.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Tool scope and write authorization\n\n### 8.1 Reads\n\nEvery read tool grows an optional `scope` argument:\n\n```python\nscope: Literal[\"own\", \"all\"] | str = \"own\"   # \"topic:<slug>\"\n```\n\nResolution against `ctx.read_scopes`:\n\n- `\"own\"` (default): filter by `ctx.primary_topic_id` via `artifact_topics`.\n- `\"all\"`: allowed only if `ctx.read_scopes.topics == \"all\"`.\n- `\"topic:<slug>\"`: allowed only if slug is in `ctx.read_scopes.topics` or `topics == \"all\"`.\n\nCross-topic reads are **explicit**, never auto-expanded on empty results. The agent opts in and the reason appears in `tool_calls.arguments`.\n\n### 8.2 Writes — gated by `write_scopes` (§19.11)\n\nWrites accept `topic_slugs: list[str]` defaulting to `[ctx.primary_topic_slug]`. The set is intersected with `ctx.write_scopes.topics` at the tool boundary; if non-trivially intersected (the agent asked to write to a topic it's not authorized for), the tool rejects.\n\nCross-topic writes (any topic other than primary) require a non-empty `reason`. The reason is stored in every created `artifact_topics` row.\n\nThis is the durable rule: **default own topic, allow configured cross-topic writes, record why every cross-topic tag exists.** Not \"agent freely overrides.\"\n\n### 8.3 The cross-topic peek block (in hot context)\n\nFor each other topic the served user(s) have activity in, when `peek` is enabled:\n\n```\n[topic: career]\n  Status (Maya, 3d ago by coach): \"Looking for a new role — anxious about timeline.\"\n  Counts for Maya: memories=12, watch_items=3, themes=2, recent_observations=5 (last 14d)\n  Counts for Liam: memories=4,  watch_items=0, themes=1, recent_observations=1\n```\n\nRules:\n\n- Counts **per-user**, not pooled.\n- Window fixed and stated (proposal: 14 days).\n- Status headline verbatim only when `allow_cross_topic_status_injection` is true; otherwise summarized to \"status present\" or omitted.\n- Contents not in the peek — agent must read explicitly.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Cross-topic awareness — why no \"bridge\" primitive\n\nStatus visible in every bot's system prompt + explicit cross-topic reads cover the use case. A coach that wants the mediator to know something updates its own status; the mediator sees it next turn. Push/ack workflows are premature.\n\nThe existing within-topic `bridge_candidates` (dyadic cross-partner) is a different concept that happens to share the word. Preserved unchanged, now with `bot_id` + `topic_id` + `dyad_id` columns (§3.1).\n\n---\n\n## 10. The Bot abstraction (code) and the full refactor surface\n\n### 10.1 BotSpec fields\n\n| Currently on `settings` | Moves to `BotSpec` |\n|---|---|\n| `bot_id` | self |\n| `assistant_name` | `bot.assistant_name` |\n| `system_prompt_version` | `bot.prompt_version` |\n| `STEP_ALLOWED_TOOLS` (global) | `bot.allowed_tools_for_step(step)` |\n| `partner_phone_a/b` | resolved via `bot_bindings` + `channels` |\n| `messaging_provider` | resolved via channel + transport |\n\nNew fields on `BotSpec`:\n\n- `primary_topic_slug`\n- `participants_shape`\n- `allowed_tools_per_step` — participant-shape specific (§5.2)\n- `tool_registry` — solo bots literally don't register dyadic tools (§19.14)\n- `read_scopes` / `write_scopes` (§6.3)\n- `hot_context_builder` — separate solo and dyadic implementations\n- `system_prompt_renderer` — separate solo and dyadic implementations\n- `crisis_handler` — per-bot\n- `onboarding_renderer` — per-bot first-contact behavior\n- `oob_guardrail` — `strict | lenient | off`\n- `cross_topic_policy` — `peek | explicit | forbidden`\n- `tool_descriptions_override` — escape hatch (see §15)\n\nAfter this refactor every per-bot decision flows from `bot_spec`. Nothing reads `settings.bot_id`.\n\n### 10.2 Full refactor list (broader than earlier drafts)\n\nBeyond the spec itself, multi-bot reaches into:\n\n- **Burst coalescer** keyed by `(user_id, bot_id)`.\n- **Newer-inbound suppression** (§19.5): keyed by `(sender_id, bot_id)` not just `sender_id`. Without this, a finance bot message can cancel the mediator's outbound. Affects `agentic.py:612`, `read_tools.py:166`.\n- **Outbound delivery** uses the bot's transport via channel (no inline `messaging_provider` switch).\n- **OOB guardrail** at delivery: filter to `bot_topic` membership in `artifact_topics`, or globally-scoped OOB (no rows in `artifact_topics`).\n- **Scheduled job dispatcher** resolves `bot_id` from the row, fires that bot's loop.\n- **Onboarding** (§19.9): per-bot welcome text, per-bot first-turn behavior. Hard-coded mediator welcome in `inbound.py:23` becomes `bot_spec.onboarding_renderer.welcome()`. `users.onboarding_state` migrates to `user_bot_state(user_id, bot_id, onboarding_state, paused, …)`.\n- **Pause/resume** (§19.6): per-(user, bot) in `user_bot_state`. **Global pause is preserved as a separate kill switch** — `system_state.is_paused` stays as the platform-wide brake; the per-(user, bot) state is additive, not a replacement.\n- **`consult_perspective`** (§19.7): clones `TurnContext` preserving scopes, primary topic, and policy. Cross-topic reads from consult respect the same authorization.\n- **Prompt renderer**: split into solo and dyadic implementations rather than partner-optional one renderer with dead policy.\n- **Hot context builder**: split likewise.\n- **`TurnContext.partner`** becomes `Optional[User]`; the type change is small, the rewrites in hot context and prompts are not.\n- **Telemetry / logs** include `bot_id`, `topic_id`, `binding_id` on every event.\n- **Evals**: per-bot suites, no reuse across bots.\n- **Tests / fixtures**: take a `bot_spec`; default mediator fixture stays for back-compat.\n\n### 10.3 Audit versioning on `bot_turns` (§19.8)\n\n`bot_turns` adds `bot_id` *and* pinned versions of every load-bearing piece:\n\n- `bot_spec_version` — content hash or version tag of the code-defined spec\n- `system_prompt_version` — already exists, kept\n- `hot_context_builder_version` — version tag of the builder used\n- `tool_schema_version` — global version of `tool_schemas.py`\n\nThis is what enables \"why did the bot answer this way on 2026-04-12\" six months from now.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Code vs data config\n\n**Code** (versioned with source):\n\n- System prompts, step instructions\n- Allowed tool sets, tool implementations\n- Crisis handlers, hot context builders, onboarding renderers\n- `BotSpec` instances\n\n**Data** (changeable without deploy):\n\n- `topics`, `bots`, `channels`, `dyads`, `dyad_members`, `bot_bindings`\n- `user_bot_state` (onboarding + pause/resume)\n- `user_identities` (§12)\n\n`bots` rows are thin pointers to code-defined `BotSpec`. Ops can register a bot or rebind a channel without code changes; behavior stays in version control.\n\n---\n\n## 12. Channels, routing, and user identity\n\nThe doc previously punted user identity to \"phase 4+.\" That was wrong (§19.16, §19.18) — multi-transport breaks identity before the second bot is useful. Identity lands in phase 0/1.\n\n### 12.1 Channels\n\nA **channel** is any addressable inbound surface a bot listens on. Today: a Discord bot account or a phone number. Tomorrow: a Discord mention in a guild channel, a Slack app, etc.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE channels (\n  id         uuid PRIMARY KEY,\n  bot_id     text NOT NULL REFERENCES bots(id),\n  transport  text NOT NULL,                      -- 'discord' | 'whatsapp' | …\n  address    text NOT NULL,                      -- bot account id, phone number, …\n  guild_id   text,                               -- transport-specific\n  channel_id text,\n  config     jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,\n  UNIQUE (transport, address, guild_id, channel_id)\n);\n```\n\nThe routing primitive: `resolve_bot(inbound_event) -> bot_id`. Channels table is the lookup; keys are transport-specific. No code path assumes 1:1.\n\n### 12.2 User identity across transports\n\nToday `users.phone` is reused for Discord ids (`discord.py:176` vs `migrations/0001_init.sql:10`). For multi-bot, a single human may reach the coach via Discord and the mediator via WhatsApp; we need a way to know \"same person.\"\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE user_identities (\n  user_id    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),\n  transport  text NOT NULL,\n  address    text NOT NULL,\n  verified_at timestamptz,\n  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),\n  PRIMARY KEY (transport, address)\n);\n```\n\nSender resolution at inbound becomes: `(transport, address)` lookup against `user_identities`, returning `user_id`. The legacy `users.phone` column is migrated to a `(transport='legacy', address=<phone>)` row in phase 0 and the field is no longer load-bearing.\n\nAccount-linking (a human verifying \"this Discord id and that WhatsApp number are me\") is a workflow we don't build yet but the schema is ready for. Until linking happens, two transport identities are two `user_id`s. The risk of writing memories/OOB/feedback under duplicate humans is real and the schema lets us merge later without rewriting encrypted blobs.\n\n### 12.3 Inbound flow\n\n1. Webhook receives event; extract transport identity.\n2. `resolve_bot(event) -> bot_id`.\n3. Sender resolution → `user_id` via `user_identities`.\n4. Resolve `bot_spec`; resolve `binding` from `bot_bindings`.\n5. For dyadic: confirm sender is a dyad member; set `user_in_context`.\n6. For solo: confirm sender is the bound user.\n7. Inbound `messages` row stamped with `bot_id`, `topic_id`, `user_in_context`, `channel_id`.\n8. Burst coalesce by `(user_id, bot_id)`.\n9. Construct `TurnContext` with all scope fields populated (§6.1).\n10. `bot_turns` created with `bot_id`, `topic_id`, version pins.\n\n---\n\n## 13. Tool descriptions\n\n**Decision: genericize.** Tool descriptions say what the tool does (\"record a durable fact about a user\"); per-bot framing belongs in the system prompt and step instructions. `BotSpec.tool_descriptions_override` exists as an escape hatch; should be unused at first.\n\nThis works in combination with §5.2 enforcement: a coach simply has fewer tools registered, rather than the same tool described differently.\n\n---\n\n## 14. Hot context\n\n`build_hot_context` is a **per-bot** callable: `bot_spec.hot_context_builder(...)`. Solo and dyadic builders are separate implementations (§19.14), not one partner-optional builder.\n\nEvery builder must include:\n\n- **Status block** for the bot's own topic, for the served user(s) and pair (if dyadic).\n- **Cross-topic status block** *only if* `ctx.read_scopes.allow_cross_topic_status_injection` is true.\n- **Cross-topic peek block** *only if* `ctx.cross_topic_policy == \"peek\"` and `ctx.read_scopes.allow_cross_topic_peek` is true.\n- **OOB block** filtered to global OOB + own-topic OOB.\n\nBot-specific:\n\n- **Dyadic builder** bins artifacts into three buckets (about A / about B / shared).\n- **Solo builder** has one bucket (about the user).\n- Selection, ordering, domain framing per bot.\n\nStyle notes are global to the user.\n\n---\n\n## 15. Crisis handling\n\nPluggable on `BotSpec`:\n\n- `detect_crisis(message_text, context) -> CrisisLevel | None`\n- `handle_crisis(level, ctx) -> CrisisAction`\n\nThe mediator's existing drop-role behavior is one implementation. A **solo bot** needs its own answer: it can't escalate to a partner. Default for solo bots: refer the user to their dyadic bot (if a binding exists for them), plus surface external resources. Per-bot can override.\n\n---\n\n## 16. Migration plan\n\nRe-phased after the verification passes. **Phase 0 is genuinely no-op**: schema is additive and nullable; insert sites untouched; mediator behaves identically. **Phase 1 ships insert-site changes and applies NOT NULL.**\n\n### Phase 0 — additive schema, no behavior change (no NOT NULL)\n\n1. `CREATE TABLE topics`; insert `relationship` row.\n2. `CREATE TABLE bots`; insert `mediator` row (`primary_topic = relationship`, `participants_shape = 'dyad'`).\n3. `CREATE TABLE dyads`; insert one row for the existing pair.\n4. `CREATE TABLE dyad_members`; insert two rows.\n5. `CREATE TABLE bot_bindings`; insert `(mediator, dyad)`.\n6. `CREATE TABLE channels`; insert existing Discord bot account / phone records pointing at `mediator`.\n7. `CREATE TABLE user_identities`; migrate `users.phone` into `(transport='legacy', address=<phone>)`. Legacy `phone` column kept for reads during transition.\n8. `CREATE TABLE artifact_topics` (join table for multi-topic membership).\n9. Backfill `artifact_topics`: one row per `(memories|themes|observations|watch_items|distillations|out_of_bounds, id)` × `relationship` topic. `tagged_by_bot_id = 'mediator'`, `reason = 'backfill'`, `status = 'active'`.\n10. Add nullable columns to single-topic tables: `topic_id uuid NULL` on `messages`, `bot_turns`, `scheduled_jobs`, `feedback`, `bridge_candidates`; `bot_id text NULL` (FK to `bots` with `ON DELETE RESTRICT`) on same; `dyad_id uuid NULL` on `bridge_candidates`.\n11. Add `recorded_by_bot_id text NULL` (FK to `bots`) to artifact tables.\n12. Add audit columns to `bot_turns`: `bot_spec_version`, `hot_context_builder_version`, `tool_schema_version` (all nullable).\n13. Backfill: all existing rows get `bot_id = 'mediator'`, `topic_id = <relationship_id>`, `dyad_id = <single_dyad_id>` on bridges, `recorded_by_bot_id = 'mediator'`.\n14. `CREATE TABLE topic_status` with the two partial unique indexes from §7.\n15. `CREATE TABLE user_bot_state`; populate from current `users.onboarding_state` for `bot_id='mediator'`.\n16. Validation queries: assert no `messages.bot_id IS NULL`, no `artifact_topics` gaps, etc. Stored in `migrations/validation/0xxx_phase0_validation.sql`.\n\n**Phase 0 ships with all NULLs allowed and no insert sites changed. Mediator behaves identically.**\n\n### Phase 1 — insert-site updates + NOT NULL + `BotSpec` refactor\n\n1. Update insert sites to stamp the new columns:\n   - `app/services/inbound.py:161` — write `bot_id`, `topic_id`, `channel_id` on inbound messages.\n   - `app/services/messaging.py:55,84` — same on outbound.\n   - `app/services/agentic.py:483` — write `bot_id`, `topic_id`, `bot_spec_version`, `hot_context_builder_version`, `tool_schema_version` on `bot_turns`.\n   - Tool write paths stamp `recorded_by_bot_id` and create `artifact_topics` rows.\n2. `TurnContext` carries scope fields (§6.1).\n3. `BotSpec` absorbs per-bot config; `agentic.py` resolves `bot_spec` from inbound routing (not `settings`).\n4. Burst coalescer keyed by `(user_id, bot_id)`.\n5. Newer-inbound suppression keyed by `(sender_id, bot_id)`.\n6. Outbound delivery uses the bot's transport via channel.\n7. Scheduled-job dispatcher resolves bot from row.\n8. Tests/fixtures take a `bot_spec`.\n9. **After cutover with monitoring**, apply NOT NULL on `messages.bot_id`, `topic_id`; `bot_turns.bot_id`, `topic_id`; etc.\n\n### Phase 2 — read scopes + authorization\n\n1. Add `scope` to read tools; default `\"own\"`.\n2. Tool boundary validates against `ctx.read_scopes`.\n3. `consult_perspective` inherits scopes structurally.\n4. `cross_topic_policy` honored in hot context (peek block, status injection).\n\n### Phase 3 — write scopes + multi-topic writes via join table\n\n1. Write tools accept `topic_slugs`; default `[primary]`.\n2. Tool boundary validates against `ctx.write_scopes`; cross-topic writes require `reason`.\n3. Inserts create `artifact_topics` rows.\n\n### Phase 4 — topic status\n\n1. `set_topic_status` tool, status block in hot context (policy-gated).\n2. Mediator starts setting per-user and pair statuses.\n3. Record-step instructions updated to prompt status review.\n\n### Phase 5 — second bot (solo)\n\n1. New `BotSpec` (e.g. `app/bots/coach.py`), new prompt renderer (solo), new hot context builder (solo), new onboarding renderer.\n2. New `topic` row, `bot` row, `channel` row, `bot_binding` row.\n3. Generic tool descriptions already in place; solo bot has dyadic tools un-registered.\n\n### Phase 6 — second dyadic bot (if/when)\n\nRepeats phase 5 patterns but with dyadic shape. Reuses existing `dyads`/`dyad_members`. New `bot_binding` to existing or new dyad.\n\n### Phase 7 — optional\n\nAccount-linking workflow surfacing in UI. Status history. Cross-bot bridge primitive if ever needed.\n\n---\n\n## 17. Risks\n\n- **Scope enforcement is the security model.** Every leak path runs through a tool that didn't consult `ctx.read_scopes`/`ctx.write_scopes`. Centralize the check; add a lint that rejects DB queries in tools that don't pass through the authorization layer.\n- **`artifact_topics` migration is the largest single migration.** Backfilling memories/observations/themes/watch_items/distillations/OOB rows on a hot DB needs batching and validation queries.\n- **OOB nullable membership semantics.** Global OOB is \"no row in `artifact_topics`.\" Make this loud in code review.\n- **Newer-inbound suppression cutover.** Re-keying mid-deploy will briefly let stale sends through. Drain or use a feature flag.\n- **Channel routing is security-sensitive.** Startup integrity check: every channel resolves to a known bot; FK with `ON DELETE RESTRICT`.\n- **Prompt token budget.** Status + peek compound with topic count. Cap peek to N most-recently-active topics; enforce headline ≤ 80 chars, body ≤ 300; cap injected statuses.\n- **Identity duplication risk before linking lands.** A human reaching two bots on two transports may be two `user_id`s for a while. Memories/OOB/feedback under both. Linking workflow (phase 7) must support merging without rewriting encrypted blobs — the schema is built for this but the workflow isn't free.\n- **Global pause + per-(user, bot) pause** interact non-trivially. Document precedence: global pause wins, per-(user, bot) is additive.\n- **Solo bot crisis defaults.** Generic default exists; flag at each new solo bot creation that this needs review.\n- **Out of scope but worth flagging**: per-bot spend caps, per-bot eval baselines, admin UI filters, RLS policies, GDPR delete/export semantics across topics (each user's memories live in many `artifact_topics` rows now). All deferred but named.\n\n---\n\n## 18. Decisions confirmed and remaining open\n\n### Confirmed\n\n1. 1:1 bot↔topic to start; schema-ready for many-to-1.\n2. OOB topic membership via `artifact_topics`; no rows = global.\n3. `topic_status` keyed by `(topic, user)` or `(topic, dyad)`; mutual exclusion via CHECK.\n4. Mediator's `cross_topic_policy = \"peek\"`; status injection allowed for own topic always, cross-topic gated by `allow_cross_topic_status_injection`.\n5. Tool descriptions: genericize universally; per-bot override only as escape hatch.\n6. # Sprint plan — multi-agent architecture

**Framing.** I think §16's seven "phases" map roughly to six 2-week sprints, not seven. Phases 5 and 6 collapse (one is the deliverable, one is "do it again") and phase 7 is genuinely deferred. I disagree with §16 on two points: (1) phase 0 is too light as written — it should bundle code-level prep so phase 1 doesn't carry both an insert-site cutover AND a `BotSpec` refactor AND `TurnContext` retyping AND NOT NULL; (2) phase 1 as described is two sprints' worth of work and must be split. The cut I propose is **state-stamping first, behavior-policing second**.

I'll call the topic-join migration its own sprint. It deserves it.

---

## Sprint 1: Foundation schema + code shape, zero behavior change

**Goal.** Land every additive table, backfill, and the code skeletons (`TurnContext` fields, `BotSpec` carrier fields, channel/binding/identity resolution helpers) so that subsequent sprints only flip switches.

**Pre-flight context.**
- Read `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/migrations/0001_init.sql`, `0013_bridge_candidates.sql`, `0015_distillations.sql`, `0017_scheduled_tasks.sql` to confirm column shapes against §3.
- Read `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/inbound.py` lines around 23, 136, 161 and `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/messaging.py:55,84,155,338,370`.
- Confirm open decisions A (peek window = 14d), C (solo crisis default), D (status cap N) — D doesn't block; A and C don't bite until S4/S5. Push back on locking these until needed.
- Confirm decision on `users.phone` → `user_identities` backfill semantics: do legacy Discord-id-in-phone rows become `transport='discord'` or `transport='legacy'`? Design doc says `legacy`; verify nothing in `discord.py:176` actively writes to `users.phone` going forward.
- Snapshot a pg `pg_dump --schema-only` of prod for rollback comparison.

**Work items, ordered.**
1. Migration `0020_topics_bots_bindings.sql`: `topics`, `bots`, `dyads`, `dyad_members`, `bot_bindings`, `channels`, `user_identities`. Seed `relationship` topic, `mediator` bot row, one `dyads` row, two `dyad_members`, one `bot_bindings`, channel rows for current Discord + WhatsApp. Backfill `user_identities` from `users.phone`.
2. Migration `0021_artifact_topics.sql`: create the join table + the two partial indexes from §2.
3. Migration `0022_topic_status_user_bot_state.sql`: `topic_status` (both partial indexes from §7), `user_bot_state` populated from `users.onboarding_state` for `mediator`.
4. Migration `0023_nullable_scope_columns.sql`: nullable `topic_id`, `bot_id` on `messages`, `bot_turns`, `scheduled_jobs`, `feedback`, `bridge_candidates`; `dyad_id` on `bridge_candidates`; `recorded_by_bot_id` on artifact tables; audit columns on `bot_turns`.
5. Migration `0024_backfill.sql` — batched (`UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT ... LIMIT 5000)` in loop) for any table over ~50k rows. Validation queries committed to `migrations/validation/`.
6. Code: extend `app/services/turn_context.py` with `bot_id`, `bot_spec`, `binding_id`, `participants_shape`, `primary_topic_id`, `primary_topic_slug`, `channel_id`, `read_scopes`, `write_scopes`, `cross_topic_policy` — **all optional with defaults**. Make `partner: User | None`. Code that currently dereferences `partner` is untouched — defaults keep it non-None for now.
7. Code: extend `app/bots/base.py` BotSpec with the new fields as optional with mediator-shaped defaults. Add `ReadScopes`/`WriteScopes` dataclasses. No call-site changes.
8. Code: new module `app/services/routing.py` with `resolve_bot(event)`, `resolve_sender(transport, address)`, `resolve_binding(bot_id, user_id)`. **Not wired into inbound yet.** Unit tests cover them.
9. Code: registry-aware `MEDIATOR_BOT` carries the new fields populated from DB at startup.

Dependencies: (1) gates (2,3,4); (4) gates (5); (6,7,8,9) parallel to migrations as long as no call sites change.

**Mid-sprint checkpoint (day 5–6).**
- All migrations applied to a staging clone of prod with full row counts.
- `SELECT count(*) FROM artifact_topics` equals sum of (memories + themes + observations + watch_items + distillations + out_of_bounds) row counts.
- `SELECT count(*) FROM messages WHERE bot_id IS NULL` is zero.
- `SELECT count(*) FROM user_identities WHERE transport='legacy'` equals `count(*) FROM users WHERE phone IS NOT NULL`.
- Mediator runs against the migrated staging DB with **no code changes** and a clean turn completes end-to-end. **If this fails, the additive migration isn't actually additive — stop and find the FK or trigger that broke.**

**Definition of done.**
- All migrations live in prod. Backfill validated. Mediator's behavior in prod is byte-for-byte identical (compare `bot_turns.prompt_snapshot` hashes between two equivalent turns pre- and post-migration on a canary).
- `TurnContext`, `BotSpec`, `routing.py` shipped with the new fields populated by default constructors. No call site references the new fields yet.
- Zero new NOT NULLs.

**Risks.**
- Backfilling `artifact_topics` on a hot DB is the largest write of the sprint. Batch + advisory-lock or accept lag. Schedule for off-hours.
- The `users.phone` → `user_identities` backfill is single-row-per-user; if any user has both a phone and a Discord id stored in `phone`, both must become identity rows. Audit before backfill.
- `bot_bindings` CHECK constraint mistake (`(user_id IS NOT NULL) <> (dyad_id IS NOT NULL)`) is one typo from blocking inserts. Test the CHECK in CI.

**Not in this sprint.**
- Any insert site writes the new columns. Any NOT NULL. Any read of `artifact_topics`. Any scope check. Any second bot.

## Sprint 2: Stamp the columns, flip NOT NULL, but no policy change

**Goal.** Insert sites write the new columns; reads still ignore them; mediator still behaves identically.

**Pre-flight context.**
- Confirm Sprint 1 backfill held over a week with no orphan rows.
- Read `app/services/agentic.py:483, 612, 725` and `app/services/tools/write_tools.py` insert blocks. Note every `INSERT INTO memories|themes|observations|watch_items|distillations|out_of_bounds` site.

**Work items, ordered.**
1. Wire `routing.py` into `inbound.py:23-180`. Resolve bot/binding/topic; populate `TurnContext` with real scope fields (defaults to mediator/relationship for now).
2. Update `inbound.py:161` outbound insert: stamp `bot_id`, `topic_id`, `channel_id`.
3. Update `messaging.py:55,84` outbound stamping.
4. Update `agentic.py:483` `bot_turns` insert: `bot_id`, `topic_id`, `bot_spec_version` (hash of `BotSpec` repr), `hot_context_builder_version` (string constant in builder module), `tool_schema_version` (hash of `tool_schemas.py`).
5. Update every artifact write in `write_tools.py` to stamp `recorded_by_bot_id` AND create `artifact_topics` row(s) for the bot's primary topic.
6. Rekey burst coalescer to `(user_id, bot_id)` — `app/services/debouncer.py` or wherever, find it via grep.
7. Rekey newer-inbound suppression `(sender_id, bot_id)` at `agentic.py:612` and `read_tools.py:166`.
8. Scheduled-job dispatcher (`app/services/scheduled_jobs.py`) reads `bot_id` from row, fires that bot's loop. With one bot this is a no-op.
9. Migration `0025_apply_not_null.sql` — set NOT NULL on `messages.bot_id, topic_id`, `bot_turns.bot_id, topic_id`, the others — **only after a soak period within the sprint.** Day 8–9.
10. Tests/fixtures take a `bot_spec` argument (default mediator).

Dependencies: (1) gates (2-7); soak day 1–7 before (9).

**Mid-sprint checkpoint (day 5–6).**
- Production has been writing `bot_id`/`topic_id` on every new row for ≥48h.
- `SELECT count(*) FROM messages WHERE created_at > now() - interval '24h' AND bot_id IS NULL` is zero.
- `SELECT count(*) FROM artifact_topics WHERE created_at > now() - interval '24h'` is non-zero and matches new artifact write count.
- **If any new row has NULL where it shouldn't:** find the missed insert site before applying NOT NULL.

**Definition of done.**
- All NOT NULLs applied. Burst coalescer + newer-inbound suppression keyed per-bot in prod. Tool writes create `artifact_topics` rows in lockstep with artifact INSERTs. Audit columns populated on every `bot_turns`.

**Risks.**
- Newer-inbound suppression rekey is the worst cutover risk in the whole project. **During cutover, briefly a stale send may slip through.** Deploy at low-traffic hour; consider a transitional version that checks BOTH old and new keys for one deploy.
- Missing an insert site means NOT NULL fails. The `grep -rn 'INSERT INTO'` sweep on day 1 must be exhaustive. Capture in a checklist file (locally, not committed) and tick off.
- An `artifact_topics` write that fails after the artifact INSERT succeeded leaves an orphan. Wrap both in a transaction.

**Not in this sprint.**
- Reading via `artifact_topics`. Scope enforcement. `BotSpec` refactor beyond carrier-fields. Solo prompt renderer. Second bot.

## Sprint 3: The `artifact_topics` join cutover for reads

**Goal.** Every read of memories/themes/observations/watch_items/distillations/OOB goes through the join. Behavior identical (mediator's primary topic is always `relationship`, so the join is a no-op filter).

**Pre-flight context.**
- Audit every `SELECT` against the six artifact tables. Grep for the table names in `app/services/hot_context.py`, `read_tools.py`, `write_tools.py`, `oob_check.py`, `cross_thread_privacy.py`, `decay.py`, any background jobs. Expect ~30–50 query sites.
- Confirm decision A (peek window 14d) — not needed yet but fix before S4.

**Work items, ordered.**
1. Add a query helper `app/services/topic_filter.py` with `join_artifact_topics(table_alias, topic_id)` returning SQL fragment. Standardizes the join.
2. Rewrite each read query to JOIN `artifact_topics` filtering by `topic_id = ctx.primary_topic_id AND status='active'`. Per file in this order: `hot_context.py` (largest), `read_tools.py`, `oob_check.py`, `cross_thread_privacy.py`, `decay.py`, `withheld_reviews.py`.
3. Add EXPLAIN regression check: a script that runs representative queries on a staging DB and asserts index usage on the partial index `(topic_id, artifact_table) WHERE status='active'`.
4. OOB delivery-time guardrail: filter to (no `artifact_topics` rows) OR (row matches `ctx.primary_topic_id`). This is the §6 "global OOB" semantic.
5. Property test or integration test that compares hot context output on a snapshot before-vs-after the join — must match exactly.

Dependencies: (1) gates (2); (2) gates (3, 5).

**Mid-sprint checkpoint (day 5–6).**
- Half the read sites converted, hot context output diff against pre-cutover is empty for a canary user.
- Query latency on staging within 10% of pre-cutover. **If a query regresses materially, fix the index or query before continuing.** The partial index design from §2 should cover us but verify.

**Definition of done.**
- Every artifact read goes through `artifact_topics`. EXPLAIN check is green. Production hot context byte-identical to pre-cutover for the active dyad (verify by hashing rendered context for a week).

**Risks.**
- Forgetting one read site means a different bot in the future sees unauthorized data. Lint check: a grep that fails CI if `FROM memories\b` appears outside `topic_filter.py` and known exceptions.
- Index scan plan regressions on memories/distillations — they're already large. Have a rollback migration ready for the indexes (the queries can stay; only the indexes might need tuning).

**Not in this sprint.**
- Multi-topic writes. Scope enforcement (`read_scopes` honored beyond hardcoded primary). Status injection. The `scope` argument on read tools.

---

## Sprint 4: Authorization on `TurnContext` — read scopes, write scopes, status

**Goal.** Add the authorization layer (§6, §8) and ship `topic_status` (§7). Mediator becomes the first bot whose behavior is governed by `read_scopes`/`write_scopes`, but its config matches today's implicit behavior.

**Pre-flight context.**
- Lock decision A (peek window): default to 14d in code with a `BotSpec` override. Don't make it global config.
- Lock decision D (status cap N): default to 5 most-recently-active topics per user.
- Lock decision B: status update folded into `record` step, per §7.5.
- Read `app/services/tools/consult_perspective.py:105-139` to plan scope inheritance.

**Work items, ordered.**
1. Implement `ReadScopes`/`WriteScopes` enforcement: every read tool consults `ctx.read_scopes`; every write consults `ctx.write_scopes`. Add `scope` parameter to read tools defaulting to `"own"`. With one topic, `"own"` and `"all"` resolve the same — verify the plumbing without changing output.
2. `consult_perspective` clones `ctx` preserving scope fields.
3. Migration: nothing schema-level new; `topic_status` already exists from S1.
4. Implement `set_topic_status` tool. Register only for `mediator` initially. Folded into `record` step instruction.
5. Hot context: add status block (own topic) for served user(s) + pair (`dyad_id` set, `user_id` NULL). Policy-gated cross-topic status injection — code path exists but with one topic, never triggers.
6. Cross-topic peek block code path — same: present but with one topic, emits nothing.
7. Add `cross_topic_policy = "peek"` to mediator's BotSpec. Mediator's `read_scopes = ReadScopes(topics={"own"}, allow_cross_topic_peek=True, allow_cross_topic_status_injection=True)`. `write_scopes = WriteScopes(topics={"relationship"}, require_reason_for_cross_topic=True)`.
8. Lint/test that asserts every DB-touching function in `read_tools.py`/`write_tools.py` accepts and uses `ctx`.

**Mid-sprint checkpoint.**
- Mediator running with the authorization layer wired but only one topic configured. `bot_turns` log unchanged in shape.
- Write a no-op second `BotSpec` in a test (not deployed) configured with `read_scopes.topics={"career"}` and verify it fails to read `relationship` artifacts. **If this fails, scope enforcement isn't real yet.**

**Definition of done.**
- Every artifact read/write checks `ctx.read_scopes`/`ctx.write_scopes`. Mediator writes status; status block renders. Negative-permission test in CI passes.

**Risks.**
- Adding `scope` to every read tool changes tool schemas → may affect model behavior. Roll out with the parameter present but undocumented in tool descriptions for one deploy, then surface it.
- Status injection token budget. Cap headline (80) and body (300) in `set_topic_status`.
- `consult_perspective` is the easiest place to leak — clone ctx, not selectively copy fields. Write a test that mutates ctx after consult and verifies the consult inherited the right fields.

**Not in this sprint.**
- Multi-topic writes via `topic_slugs`. Second bot. Solo renderer/builder. Account-linking workflow.

---

## Sprint 5: Solo bot — renderer, builder, and the first non-mediator deployment

**Goal.** Ship the second bot (solo) end to end on its own channel, with its own topic, prompt renderer, hot context builder, onboarding, crisis handler.

This is the load-bearing sprint and the riskiest. Everything before exists to make this sprint possible. The solo renderer and solo hot context builder are substantial **net-new code** (not refactors). They must be written here, not earlier — earlier they have no consumer and bit-rot.

**Pre-flight context.**
- Decision: which solo bot? Coach? Finance? Lock the prompt and tool surface with the user before sprint start.
- Decision: which transport? If new (e.g. a separate Discord bot account), provisioning lead time matters.
- Lock decision C (solo crisis default): refer to dyadic bot + external resources.
- Decision: cross_topic_policy for the new bot. Recommend `"peek"` to match mediator pattern.
- Read `app/services/prompts.py:122-186, 217-222, 335-370` (dyad-only sections to skip in solo renderer).

**Work items, ordered.**
1. `app/services/prompts_solo.py` — solo system prompt renderer. No partner placeholder, no bridges, no in-person redirect, no partner crisis escalation.
2. `app/services/hot_context_solo.py` — solo hot context builder. Single about-user bucket. Status block for own topic for the bound user. Peek block (still no other topics for *this* user unless the dyadic mediator also serves them).
3. `app/services/onboarding_solo.py` — first-contact renderer per §10.2.
4. `app/services/crisis_solo.py` — default handler that refers to dyadic bot + external resources.
5. `app/bots/coach.py` (or chosen name) — `BotSpec` instance, `participants_shape="solo"`, primary topic, tool registry that **excludes** bridge tools, `create_bridge_candidate`, in-person redirect.
6. Data: new `topics` row, `bots` row, `channels` row (new Discord bot account or phone), `bot_bindings` row pointing to a single user.
7. Tool registry: filter dyadic-only tools at registration time per `participants_shape`. This is the §5.2 enforcement bullet — solo bot literally doesn't see the tools.
8. Solo participant-shape validation in write tools: reject `about_user_id != bound_user_id`, reject `about_user_id IS NULL`.
9. End-to-end test: solo bot turn against a test user produces a response, writes a memory, writes status, attempts a bridge tool call and fails at the boundary.
10. Deploy to one consenting user. Monitor closely for a week (this is why mid-sprint checkpoint matters extra).

Dependencies: (1-4) parallel; (5) gates (6); (7-8) gate (10).

**Mid-sprint checkpoint (day 5–6).**
- Solo bot completes turns end-to-end in staging against a test user.
- Bridge tool call attempt by the solo bot raises at the tool boundary (verify the registry filter and the `participants_shape` check are both live — belt and braces).
- Mediator unaffected: a control mediator turn run side-by-side produces identical output to last week's snapshot.

**Definition of done.**
- Solo bot running in production for ≥3 days against ≥1 user. Mediator unaffected. Per-user-per-bot pause works. Onboarding flow runs on first contact.

**Risks.**
- Two bots sharing one human via `user_identities`: if the solo bot's user is also in the mediator's dyad, do they get duplicate replies? Routing must be channel-specific. Verify `resolve_bot` from channel, not from user.
- Crisis handler for solo bot is untested in prod until a real crisis. Make sure the default is at least "refuse + external resources" — never silent.
- Onboarding `user_bot_state` write race: two simultaneous first messages must not create two onboarding states. Use upsert.
- The solo prompt renderer is new code with no production trail. Pair-review the prompt explicitly with the user.

**Not in this sprint.**
- Cross-topic writes from any bot. Second dyadic bot. Account-linking UI. Status history. Admin filters.

## Sprint 6: Multi-topic writes, hardening, and the rest of §17

**Goal.** Enable multi-topic writes via `topic_slugs` + `reason` (§8.2), close out the open risk items in §17, and make the system safe to add a third bot without another foundational sprint.

**Pre-flight context.**
- Decision F (when does any bot get cross-topic write scope?): recommend "no bot at launch; mechanism only." Verify with user.
- Audit prod for: any orphan `artifact_topics` rows; any messages with NULL columns; any duplicate user identities.

**Work items, ordered.**
1. Write tools accept `topic_slugs: list[str]` defaulting to `[ctx.primary_topic_slug]`. Intersect with `ctx.write_scopes.topics`. Cross-topic writes require non-empty `reason`, stored on every created `artifact_topics` row.
2. Cross-topic peek block (real this time — solo bot's served user might appear in mediator's relationship topic, so peek can show non-empty counts).
3. Status injection cross-topic — code path was wired in S4, exercise it now: mediator sees coach's per-user status headline for shared users, gated by `allow_cross_topic_status_injection`.
4. Per-(user, bot) pause UI surface (slash command or admin endpoint). Global pause stays.
5. Telemetry: every log line includes `bot_id`, `topic_id`, `binding_id`. Dashboard split by bot.
6. Lint: a CI check that rejects any new SQL `FROM` of an artifact table outside `topic_filter.py`.
7. Per-bot eval suite scaffolding (don't fill out evals — just per-bot isolation).
8. Documentation pass: a short runbook for "add a new bot in <N> steps" — proves the architecture.

**Mid-sprint checkpoint.**
- Cross-topic write test: a coach instance configured with `write_scopes.topics={"career","relationship"}` writes to relationship with `reason="user asked mediator to remember promotion"`; `artifact_topics.reason` populated.
- Mediator → coach peek block: mediator's hot context shows coach's career status headline for the served user.

**Definition of done.**
- Multi-topic write mechanism in prod (not exercised by any active bot but available). Per-bot telemetry visible. Pause-per-(user,bot) functional. Runbook merged.

**Risks.**
- Status leakage via injection — log every cross-topic status injection event in S6 explicitly for a week to verify policy gates work.
- Adding `topic_slugs` to tool schemas changes the model surface area again; consider whether it should be hidden until a bot needs it.

**Not in this sprint.**
- Account-linking workflow. Status history. RLS. GDPR per-topic delete. Second dyadic bot (mechanically trivial after S5).

## Full sprint sequence at a glance

| # | Title | Goal | Key deliverable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Foundation schema + code shape | Additive tables and code carriers, zero behavior change | All new tables + nullable scope columns shipped, `TurnContext`/`BotSpec` retyped |
| 2 | Stamp & NOT NULL | Insert sites write columns, suppression/coalescer rekey, NOT NULL applied | Every new row scoped; old code paths idempotent |
| 3 | `artifact_topics` join cutover | All artifact reads route through join table | Reads partition-safe even with one topic |
| 4 | Authorization + topic status | Scope enforcement on `TurnContext`, `topic_status` live | Mediator behaves identically but governed by explicit scopes |
| 5 | First solo bot | Solo renderer/builder/onboarding/crisis + new bot in prod | A second bot serving a real user |
| 6 | Multi-topic writes & hardening | Cross-topic write mechanism, telemetry split, lint, runbook | Architecture ready for the third bot in days, not weeks |

## Decisions the user must make before Sprint 1 starts

1. **Which solo bot will be #2, and which transport.** Drives Sprint 5 prompt work; provisioning has lead time.
2. **`users.phone` backfill semantics.** Specifically: rows where `phone` actually holds a Discord id — `transport='discord'` or `transport='legacy'`? §12.2 says `legacy`; confirm.
3. **Soak duration before applying NOT NULL in Sprint 2.** Recommend 7 days. Confirm tolerance.
4. **Cutover window for newer-inbound suppression rekey.** Low-traffic hour, brief stale-send risk window.
5. **Cross-topic policy for the new solo bot.** Default `"peek"` matches mediator pattern.
6. **Open decision C — solo crisis default** must be locked before Sprint 5 (not Sprint 1).

Decisions A (peek window), D (status cap), E (multi-transport bots), F (cross-topic write ramp), G (`themes.about_user_id`) do **not** block Sprint 1. Defer them.

## Things I'd cut if asked to compress to fewer sprints

- **Cut Sprint 6 to its safety subset (lint + telemetry + runbook); defer multi-topic writes.** No bot at launch uses cross-topic writes (decision F). The mechanism can land when the first cross-functional bot does. This buys you one sprint and the system is still production-safe.
- **Merge Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 if you can tolerate longer migration soak inside one sprint.** This makes the sprint 3 weeks de facto. Not recommended for a one-engineer team; recommended only if calendar pressure forces it.
- **`set_topic_status` (Sprint 4) can ship before any non-mediator bot exists without urgency**; if calendar slips, move status into Sprint 5 alongside the solo bot. The peek block is also load-bearing only when ≥2 topics exist, so it can move with status.
- **What I would not cut**: Sprint 3 (the join cutover). Doing it under the pressure of an active second bot is much worse than doing it while the mediator is the only consumer. This is the single most important "do it while it's a no-op" sprint.
- **What I would not cut**: `user_identities` in Sprint 1. The duplicate-human risk (§20.18) is the single highest-cost retroactive fix. Pay it before the second bot exists.

| **S6** | Multi-topic writes + hardening | Cross-topic write mechanism, telemetry split, lint, runbook for adding bot #3. |

## Where it diverges from §16 (correctly, I think)

**Phase 1 in §16 was two sprints' worth.** Plan agent splits it: S1 lands schema + code carriers with default values (no behavior change), S2 stamps the columns and applies NOT NULL after a soak. This is the right cut — it isolates the migration risk from the code-refactor risk.

**`artifact_topics` join cutover gets its own sprint (S3).** §16 had it bundled into phase 3 with multi-topic writes. Plan agent argues — convincingly — that doing the join cutover under the pressure of an active second bot is much worse than doing it while the mediator is the only consumer. "The single most important do-it-while-it's-a-no-op sprint."

**Solo bot renderer + hot context builder land in S5, not earlier.** §16 implied they could be written in parallel earlier. Plan agent says no: written earlier they have no consumer and bit-rot. They're load-bearing, artistically substantial code; they live with the solo bot deployment.

## Decisions you need to make before S1 starts

1. **Which solo bot is #2, and which transport.** Drives S5; provisioning has lead time. You probably need to start prompt-writing in parallel during S2–S4.
2. **`users.phone` backfill: rows that actually hold Discord ids — `transport='discord'` or `transport='legacy'`?** §12 says legacy; confirm.
3. **Soak duration before NOT NULL in S2.** Recommend 7 days.
4. **Cutover window for newer-inbound suppression rekey** (brief stale-send risk window).

C (solo crisis default), A (peek window), D (status cap), F (cross-topic write ramp) don't block S1 — they can be locked just-in-time before the sprint that needs them.

## What the Plan agent would cut if compressed

- S6 to its safety subset (drop multi-topic writes; no bot needs them at launch per decision F).
- `set_topic_status` could slip from S4 to S5 if calendar pressure hits.
- **Would NOT cut:** S3 (join cutover before any second bot) and `user_identities` in S1 (identity duplication is the single highest-cost retroactive fix).

## What's load-bearing in this plan

**S3 and S5 are the sprints where most things can go wrong.** S3 because every artifact read changes; if you miss one site, a future bot leaks data. S5 because the solo bot is genuinely new behavior in production for the first time. Both deserve extra paranoia at the mid-sprint checkpoint.

**S2 has the highest deploy-time risk** (newer-inbound suppression rekey is a brief stale-send window). Lowest-traffic hour, transitional version that checks both old and new keys is the safer pattern.

The plan says \"transitional dual-key version\" — verify that's actually implementable here.\n\n4. **Migration safety.** The `artifact_topics` backfill (S1) and the NOT NULL flip (S2) are the two highest-risk DB operations. What about indirect reads (joins from messages → artifact tables, etc.)?\n\n6. **S4's authorization layer.** Adding `scope` parameter to every read tool changes tool schemas, which changes what the model sees. 309	## Sprint boundary critique
310	
311	**S2 is too large.** It combines routing cutover, insert-site stamping, artifact write transactions, coalescer rekey, newer-inbound rekey, scheduled-job bot routing, fixture churn, and `NOT NULL` (§16.2, lines 648–657). That is more than a “flip columns” sprint. Current hot-path inserts are spread across inbound messages, outbound messages, `bot_turns`, scheduled jobs, and artifact writes: inbound `messages` at [inbound.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/inbound.py:161), outbound at [messaging.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/messaging.py:55), turns at [agentic.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/agentic.py:483), deferred jobs at [agentic.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/agentic.py:577), scheduler seeds at [scheduled_jobs.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/scheduled_jobs.py:216), and scheduled-task/check-in writes in [write_tools.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/tools/write_tools.py:1367). The 7-day soak inside a 10-workday sprint leaves almost no room for finding a missed insert, fixing it, and restarting the soak.
312	
313	**S3 is probably underestimated.** The plan expects ~30–50 query sites (§16.3, line 688), which is plausible only if it includes writes, linked-ID validations, background summaries, and decay. Direct artifact reads in the named files are fewer, but the real surface is broader: hot context reads all six artifact families [hot_context.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/hot_context.py:230), [hot_context.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/hot_context.py:252), [hot_context.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/hot_context.py:276), [hot_context.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/hot_context.py:295), [hot_context.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/hot_context.py:320), [hot_context.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/hot_context.py:353); read tools add direct and indirect reads, including theme-related memory/observation lookups [read_tools.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/tools/read_tools.py:546); background summaries still count themes/watch items [scheduled_job_handlers.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/scheduled_job_handlers.py:243); and decay mutates global themes/observations/watch items without topic restriction [decay.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/decay.py:41). Treat S3 as a full data-access audit sprint, not a query helper refactor.
314	
315	**S4 is heavier than the plan says.** There are 19 read-phase tools registered [registry.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/tools/registry.py:157), and adding `scope` to “every read tool” (§16.4, line 733) means changing model-visible schemas for at least the artifact tools and deciding what not to expose for `search_messages`, `recent_activity`, `check_oob`, `get_self_model`, `list_scheduled_tasks`, and `get_bot_actions`. Some “read” surfaces live in write_tools, e.g. `list_scheduled_tasks` [write_tools.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/tools/write_tools.py:1337). This is a behavior-risk sprint, not just authorization plumbing.
316	
317	**S5 is the highest slip risk.** The plan correctly calls it load-bearing (§16.5, lines 764–767), but it still under-scopes transport provisioning, webhook setup, secrets, bot/channel routing, user consent, crisis/OOB transport testing, and operational dashboards. The current `BotSpec` still assumes a partner in prompt rendering [base.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/bots/base.py:31), and the agentic runner always calls `partner_of` before building context [agentic.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/agentic.py:686). Solo support is not just new prompt files.
318	
319	## Hidden dependencies
320	
321	S2 secretly depends on more S4-style pause/routing work than acknowledged. Pause is global in DB [system_state.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/system_state.py:23), pause supersedes every pending user-facing job globally [system_state.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/system_state.py:59), and outbound checks both global pause and user pause hooks [messaging.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/messaging.py:170). S5’s “per-(user, bot) pause works” (§16.5, line 801) cannot wait until S5 if S2 is already rekeying scheduled jobs and coalescing by bot.
322	
323	The “transitional dual-key” rekey is implementable only with care. The coalescer’s in-memory dictionaries are all keyed by `UUID user_id` [debouncer.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/debouncer.py:42), and the underlying `AsyncBurstCoalescer` key is also `user_id` [debouncer.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/debouncer.py:47). You cannot just change SQL filters; active in-memory bursts from before deploy will still flush under the old key. A safe cutover needs either drain/restart semantics or a dual reader that flushes old user-key bursts and writes new `(user, bot)` bursts. Similarly, newer-inbound suppression has two copies: final-send suppression [agentic.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/agentic.py:612) and incremental send suppression [read_tools.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/app/services/tools/read_tools.py:166). Both must filter by `bot_id`, but during cutover old rows may have `NULL bot_id`, so dual-key must mean `(bot_id = ctx.bot_id OR bot_id IS NULL for legacy boundary rows)`, not just “check old and new keys.”
